newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate eases, baht steady late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate eases, baht steady late.

text.p: Sustained moderate liquidity eased the Thai overnight interbank rate slightly to 12.25-13.00 percent late on Tuesday from 12.50-13.00 in the morning in a busy dealings, dealers said.
"We saw more balanced bids and offers from big and small banks in the afternoon as people gained more confidence to square positions," a foreign bank dealer said.

Another dealer said improved liquidity helped the interbank rate down but both the money and currency markets were awaiting the outcome of a no-confidence vote against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa later this week.
Dealers said the one-month dollar/baht swap premium hovered at about 10.00 satangs per dollar before the Tuesday close against 9.50-10.50 in the morning and 11.00-11.50 late on Monday.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar midrate at 25.38 against 25.39 on Monday.
The debate on the no-confidence motion begins tomorrow.
"Some big banks offered relatively high rates, probably because of an uncertain impact that the upcoming censure debate will have on the market," she said.
The baht stood largely unchanged from Tuesday morning at 25.388-25.392 to the dollar on thinner trading but against 25.408-25.411 late on Monday.
The baht firmed in the morning in line with major currency movement as the yen and mark strengthened against the dollar.
